title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Introduction
content: Pigmented lesions of the skin are commonly referred to as freckles. They include solar lentigo, congenital nevi, mucosal nevi, and special nevi of the palms and soles. This activity helps to differentiate the various pedal nevi from acral lentiginous melanoma clinically. Plantar melanomas are characteristically late to be diagnosed, have a poorer response to treatment, and have a significantly higher mortality rate when compared to more proximal melanomas. [1]

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Etiology
content: A severe childhood burn is strongly associated with an increased risk of melanoma, while more incremental occupational exposure does not confer an increased risk. These findings support the hypothesis that melanoma risk is primarily affected by intermittent, intense sun exposure that disrupts normal immune surveillance and destroys abnormal melanocytes. Sunburn in adolescence can damage lifelong immune surveillance and disrupt the normal apoptosis of neoplastic cells. Genetic susceptibility may also contribute to melanoma in shaded areas. As many as 1 in 10 cases of melanoma may be linked to inherited faulty genes. [2]

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Epidemiology
content: The actual increase in melanoma incidence is most likely due to an overall increase in ultraviolet (UV) light exposure. Although melanoma, in general, is thought to be rare, the incidence of melanoma worldwide is rising dramatically, and despite increased efforts at screening, mortality rates have not appreciably improved. In the United States, melanoma is the fifth leading cancer in men and the seventh in women, and its incidence has doubled in the last ten years. In a study of data (1992 to 2004), researchers found that the actual incidence of melanoma (all thicknesses and among all socioeconomic levels) is increasing the case burden. The increase is from 4.7 to 7.7 cases per 100,000 older men and from 5.5 to 13.9 cases per 100,000 females. Although 5% of all melanomas are located on the foot, pedal melanoma is relatively rare in whites. Among East Asians and individuals with darkly pigmented skin, acral lentiginous melanoma is the most common subtype. [3]

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Pathophysiology
content: Melanocytes are specialized dendritic cells derived from the neural crest that can spread over the entire body surface. This spreading ability could help account for melanoma’s ability to metastasize across tissue planes and through blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatics. This metastatic passport helps make melanoma more lethal than other skin cancers that are limited to adjacent spread. Although the foot receives less solar exposure, pedal melanoma is more lethal than even more proximal thigh melanoma. Although the 5-year survival rate for melanoma of the calf is 94%, the 5-year survival rate for foot melanoma is 77%. Acral melanoma has a significantly poorer prognosis than the other subtypes of melanoma. [4]

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- History and Physical
content: Patients may present with a changing plantar mole. However, acral melanomas typically are discovered only upon focused examination of the soles and toe webs. Anatomically, the palms and soles lack hair follicles and sebaceous glands but have many sweat ducts. The palms and soles are significantly thicker, and the pressures of walking and grasping distort regular patterns. A simple clinical evaluation, looking for asymmetry, irregular borders, color variation, diameter greater than 6 mm, and changes over time or lesion elevation, is important. Augmenting these clinical observations with dermoscopy can increase diagnostic acumen by 20%. A complete examination of the soles, toe web spaces, and nail units is an important component of a lower extremity examination. [5] [6]

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Evaluation
content: In addition to evaluating the A through E characteristics of a pigmented lesion, there are specific dermoscopic patterns to guide examination. There are 3 benign patterns and 1 malignant dermoscopic pattern to consider. The parallel furrow pattern of linear pigmentation is benign over 93.2% of the time. The fibrillar pattern with pigmented furrows and fine angulated crossing filamentous, as well as the lattice-like pigment, are benign patterns. Most importantly, the parallel ridge pattern with wide diffuse pigmentation of the ridges predicts melanoma 93.7% of the time. Violation of the normal parallel furrow pattern indicates biopsy. [7]

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Treatment / Management
content: An atypical nevus on the sole can be biopsied with a simple 2 mm punch. If initial wide excision is chosen, a 1 to 2 mm rim of normal-appearing skin, along with a cuff of subdermal fat, is recommended. Once melanoma is found by either the punch or total excisional biopsy, wider excision with surgical margins of 1cm for the 0 to 2 mm thick tumors and up to 5 cm for tumors that are over 2.1 mm in thickness can be planned. This may lead to extensive tissue loss that may require amputation. In general, small plantar melanoma excision sites are allowed to granulate. Once primary healing has taken place, plastic skin grafting and flaps can be used to restore weight-bearing function. Mohs microsurgery has been used to minimize tissue loss and preserve the integrity of the affected area. An experienced oncology team is crucial for improving outcomes. The Melanoma Staging database is based on clinical experiences with over 38,900 melanoma patients and incorporates the tumor, node, metastasis (TNM) system. It relies upon assessments of the primary tumor (T), regional lymph nodes (N), and distant metastatic sites (M). The Breslow thickness primarily determines the T and is modified by the mitotic rate of the tumor. The 10-year survival rate decreases progressively, from 96 percent with primary lesions <0.5 mm thick to 54 percent with lesions 4.01 to 6 mm thick. [8] The N or lymphatic node designation assesses regional lymph node spread and has a major negative impact on long-term survival. The sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is recommended for tumors that are equal to or greater than 0.75 mm thick. If positive, complete lymph node dissection is recommended. Adjuvant interferon-alpha is then recommended for patients with a life expectancy greater than ten years. Therapies that target T lymphocyte antigens can induce an anti-tumor immune response. Ipilimumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor that has been shown to extend survival. Complications include exacerbation of pre-existing immune disorders. Anti-programmed cell death (PD-1) monoclonal antibodies, such as nivolumab and pembrolizumab, have demonstrated more effective results than conventional drugs in clinical trials for various advanced solid tumors, including melanoma, non-small cell lung carcinoma, and renal carcinoma. The 5-year survival rate for plantar melanoma is 82% for lesions up to 1.49 mm in diameter and 0% for lesions over 3.5 mm in diameter. [9]

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Differential Diagnosis
content: The differential diagnoses for melanocytic nevi include the following: Atypical mole Basal cell carcinoma Café au lait spots Cockade nevus Cutaneous melanoma Nevi of Ota and Ito Nevus spilus Nodular lesions Pyogenic granuloma

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Pearls and Other Issues
content: Advising patients to use sunscreens, perform self-examinations, and avoid tanning beds helps prevent melanoma of all types. Early detection through a comprehensive lower extremity examination, aided by dermoscopy, should reduce the time to acral melanoma diagnosis and improve survival. [10]

title: Melanocytic Nevi(Archived) -- Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
content: The diagnosis and management of melanocytic nevi are best accomplished with an interprofessional team that includes pharmacists and nurses; the latter 2 play a crucial role in educating the public about prevention. If melanocytic nevi are not diagnosed, the prognosis is poor. Thus, to improve patient outcomes, a thorough exam of the skin is vital. Patients may present with a changing plantar mole. Acral melanomas typically are discovered only upon focused examination of the soles and toe webs. A simple clinical evaluation, looking for asymmetry, irregular borders, color variation, diameter greater than 6 mm, and changes over time or lesion elevation, is important. If there is ever a doubt about a skin lesion, a biopsy should be performed.
